claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me:

**How many children are you responsible for?**

Once I know this, I'll ask you some questions about each child to assess your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm responsible for one child. My son Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you some questions to determine your eligibility.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful.

**Do you live with Alex, or are you making financial contributions towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. I do help out a bit though - I contribute towards his upkeep when I can.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. That's useful to know. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your contributions better to determine if you can continue to receive Child Benefit.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month, and what does it cover (for example, food, clothes, pocket money, or housing)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £10 a week. It's not much, but I help out with things like clothes and bits and pieces when he needs them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to check one more important thing.

**Who currently receives Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one final question to complete my assessment:

**How long has Alex been living with someone else rather than with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living with his mum for quite a while now - it's been the arrangement for a few years.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation based on the Child Benefit rules:

According to the rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can normally get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after the child goes to live with them (if nobody else claims). However, it can continue for longer if you make contributions to your child's upkeep that are at least equal to the Child Benefit payment amount.

Currently, the Child Benefit payment is £21.80 per week for the first child. You've told me you're contributing approximately £10 per week towards Alex's upkeep (clothes and bits and pieces). This is less than the Child Benefit payment amount of £21.80 per week.

Since you've been making this arrangement for a few years (well beyond the initial 8 weeks), and your contributions of £10 per week are below the required amount of £21.80 per week to continue eligibility, you would not currently be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

However, if you were able to increase your contributions to at least £21.80 per week or more, you could potentially become eligible again. You should contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your specific circumstances and any options available to you.
